Description: Senior Software Engineer, Decision Science About the Company In the coming decades, our world needs far more critical minerals including copper, lithium, and cobalt, to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. The mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered. KoBold is the leading scientific mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to discover the minerals the world needs—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. Our multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, engineers, and geologists work together to build data systems, design new sensors, and establish industry-leading workflows to develop and test subsurface predictions on our exploration projects. Our first discovery, Mingomba, is a high-grade copper deposit in Zambia, found after spending materially less than industry average. We are developing Mingomba with the same technical rigor that we apply to exploration. The Mingomba team brings together mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, and community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. By combining industry knowledge and cutting edge technology, we are developing Mingomba into a world class project that has safer and more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. It is expected to create thousands of good jobs for generations. KoBold runs exploration programs in eight countries, all with the potential for another discovery. KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi. About the Role At KoBold we believe that a modern scientific computing stack will enable systematic mineral exploration and materially improve our rate of mineral discovery. This role is a key ingredient to this strategy. As a member of our scientific computing team, you will apply decision science techniques in order to build scalable systems to help make high-speed, high-quality decisions for our mineral exploration projects. Collaborating with our exceptional team of data scientists, software engineers, and geologists, you will tackle complex scientific problems head-on and collectively pave the way for discoveries of vital energy transition metals like lithium, copper, nickel, and cobalt. Together we can shape the future of mineral exploration and contribute to building a sustainable world. Responsibilities Architect, implement, and maintain decision science libraries that will be used in KoBold’s mineral exploration analyses. Build tooling to increase the velocity of our decision making, including enabling rapid prototyping in Jupyter notebooks; build experimentation, evaluation, and simulation frameworks; turning successful R&D into robust, scalable pipelines; and organizing ML models and their outputs for repeatability and discoverability. Apply–and coach team members to use–engineering best practices such as writing robust, testable and composable code Collaborate with data scientists, geoscientists and engineers to invent the modern decision science technology for mineral exploration Occasional travel to exploration sites around the world to observe the impact of scientific computing on KoBold’s exploration products and design new technologies to further discovery. Travel is approximately twice per year depending on project needs. Qualifications Our ideal candidate will have: At least 5 years of experience in the field of decision science with a strong software engineering focus, though most great candidates will have closer to 10. Track record of building production quality data processing solutions or tooling that have delivered business value Proficiency with foundational concepts of ML, including statistical, traditional and deep-learning approaches Proficiency in Python, ideally including array-based packages such as xarray and numpy Deep experience with measured scientific data Experience in visualizing scientific data for domain experts Experience in MLops and in the making of robust ML systems Drive to increase the velocity and effectiveness of our data scientists in both experimental and production workflows Capacity to dive deep on novel challenging problems in applying decision science to mineral exploration, including understanding a complex domain of geology and mineral exploration practices as well as working with limited, disparate and noisy data sources Collaborative attitude to work with stakeholders with different backgrounds (data scientists, geoscientists, software engineers, operations) Work practices and motivation: Ability to take ownership and responsibility of large projects. Intellectual curiosity and eagerness to learn about all aspects of mineral exploration, particularly in the geology domain. Open to working directly with geologists in the field. Enjoys constantly learning such that you are driving insights and innovations. Ability to explain technical problems to and collaborate on solutions with domain experts who aren’t software developers. A strong communicator who enjoys working with colleagues across the company. Excitement about joining a fast-growing early-stage company, comfort with a dynamic work environment, and eagerness to take on a range of responsibilities. Keen not just to build cool technology, but to figure out what technical product to build to best achieve the business objectives of the company. Ability to independently prioritize multiple tasks effectively. What to Expect Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. All employees are expected to travel to project sites, with a minimum of one week per year. Field-facing and technical roles spend significantly more time in the field. Support requirements management and analysis using IBM DOORS or comparable requirements management tools. Review software behavior and implementation as necessary to support test development and anomaly investigation. Collaborate with development engineers throughout verification and certification activities. Support analysis of system performance and navigation related functionality. Participate in technical reviews involving software, hardware, systems engineering, and certification stakeholders. Participate in peer reviews of requirements, test cases, procedures, results, and verification artifacts. Support reporting program and technical status activities as required. Direct experience supporting DO-178C software development, verification, testing, or certification activities . Demonstrated experience developing and executing requirements-based software test cases and procedures. Experience supporting avionics certification and testing activities. Experience with navigation avionics, aircraft navigation systems, inertial navigation systems, or closely related aviation systems. Experience with FAA certification activities, aircraft safety analysis, or other safety critical aviation development processes. Ability to analyze software and system requirements and translate requirements into executable verification activities. Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills. Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to software quality. Strong written and verbal technical communication skills. Ability to work independently within a remote engineering environment. This is not about adding AI features to a traditional development process, it is a fundamental shift in how we build and ship software. Our target is Level 4 AI maturity: humans define the architecture, usage scenarios, and acceptance criteria, while AI agents autonomously write, review, and fix code. The AI Native Senior Software Engineer is a senior engineering role for builders who already work this way and can set the standard for others to follow. You are not writing every line of code by hand, you are orchestrating AI agents to do it, auditing their output, and ensuring the result meets the architectural and quality standards of the codebase. This is explicitly not a “vibe-coding” role. At senior level, you also carry accountability for the technical decisions and AI-native practices of your stream, not just your own output. This role requires a different profile to a traditional senior software engineer. You must have the engineering maturity to recognise when AI-generated code is correct, performant, and secure, and the judgement to know when it is not, at a level that lets you set standards others follow. You must be comfortable providing constructive, architectural feedback to AI tools the same way a senior engineer coaches a junior developer, with patience, precision, and clear expectations, and you must be equally comfortable coaching human engineers in how to do the same. decisions within your product stream, and act as an escalation point for complex technical judgement calls Set and maintain test coverage standards, ensuring AI-generated code is consistently accompanied by appropriate automated tests across the stream Debug and resolve the most complex issues across the stack, leveraging both manual investigation and AI-assisted diagnostic techniques Description: NVIDIA is redefining accelerated computing and powering the next era of artificial intelligence. Our data-center platforms bring together GPUs, CPUs, networking, systems, and software to solve some of the world’s most exciting computing problems. We are looking for a Senior System Software Engineer to join NVIDIA ’s Datacenter Performance and Power Management Software team. You will be responsible for architecting production software for datacenter power management controllers. Your work will also cover cluster- level dynamic provisioning and power-management control system technologies for next-generation data-centers. You will work at the intersection of hardware architecture, embedded firmware, device drivers, operating systems, and AI workloads. Your responsibilities will span the entire product lifecycle—from initial architectural design and pre-silicon validation through silicon bring-up, productization, and deployment in extensive data-center infrastructures. This is an outstanding chance to influence how next-generation NVIDIA GPUs provide top-tier performance, energy efficiency, and reliability. What You’ll Be Doing: Architect, build, implement, and debug data center power and performance-management software, with particular emphasis on end-to-end power management at racks and data halls. Develop real-time controllers, policies, and mechanisms that dynamically optimize performance, power, thermals, and energy efficiency under demanding data-center workloads. Drive features across the full product lifecycle: requirements, architecture, implementation, pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, productization, and production support. Collaborate with GPU architects and hardware designers to define hardware-software interfaces and influence the power-management capabilities of next-generation processors. Analyze complex interactions among workloads, clocks, voltages, power limits, thermals, telemetry, and system-level policies. Lead the investigation and resolution of complex power, performance, stability, and reliability issues spanning firmware, drivers, hardware, and platform software. Develop validation strategies and automation for functional correctness, transition latency, performance-per-watt, and robustness across operating conditions. Build clear architecture, interface, and compose specifications for new power-management features. Partner with geographically distributed architecture, ASIC, firmware, driver, validation, platform, and data-center systems teams. What We Need to See: BS or MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field—or equivalent experience. At least 12+ years of extensive industry experience crafting system software, embedded firmware, device drivers, or other hardware-related production software. Strong programming skills in C, including experience developing, debugging, and maintaining complex low-level software. Deep understanding of operating-system fundamentals, device-driver architecture, embedded or real-time software, concurrency, interrupt handling, and hardware programming. Experience interpreting hardware specifications and developing software interfaces for registers, telemetry, interrupts, and control mechanisms. Strong understanding of computer architecture and hardware-software interactions. Proven ability to independently debug complex problems across multiple software and hardware layers. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of working effectively across organizational and geographic boundaries. Ways to Stand Out From the Crowd: Background with architecting, designing, or implementing datacenter provisioning, monitoring, and managing power at a CSP/NCP. Hands-on experience with GPU, CPU, accelerator, or SoC power and performance management. Background with crafting or implementing P-state selection, DVFS, clock-control, voltage-control, power-capping, thermal-management, throttling, or workload-aware control policies. Experience developing real-time feedback controllers, including reasoning about stability, responsiveness, hysteresis, latency, and noisy telemetry. Understanding of electrical and platform considerations such as voltage-frequency relationships, transient power, thermal limits, power delivery, and system-level power budgets. Description: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. At Canonical , we are driving the engineering discipline needed to build secure, reliable, and high-quality products that our automotive and industrial partners can depend on. Ubuntu is already the world’s most widely used Linux distribution in general; we want to make it the world’s best choice for the automotive and industrial sectors too. We operate at the boundary between upstream open source innovation and the industrial regulatory realities. Our engineers define the concepts, architectures, processes, verification strategies, and certification artifacts to transform a general-purpose platform into a dependable, certifiable foundation for automotive and industrial compute. This is systems-level engineering at scale, requiring precision, rigor, and a deep understanding of how complex software behaves in constrained, regulated environments. We are looking for engineers and architects who combine an open source hacker and builder mindset with respect for rigorous, standards-driven engineering. You will work across Canonical engineering teams and with leading industrial partners, helping to build this capability from the ground up and shaping how open source enters the most demanding technical domains. Drive the creation of structured engineering artifacts, including requirements, traceability models, risk analysis, test strategies, and certification documentation. Collaborate with Canonical engineering teams to align development practices with industrial compliance needs. Design, implement, and execute verification and validation activities required to qualify Ubuntu and other components for regulated environments. Develop and improve automation and tooling to scale traceability, testing, compliance evidence generation, and reporting. Engage with industrial partners to understand their expectations, align external expectations and internal capabilities, and support audits and technical reviews. Contribute to the continuous improvement of Canonical ’s internal processes and standards capability as the team scales. What we are looking for in you Strong software engineering foundation with experience in developing complex systems on Linux. Professional experience with C, C++, and Python in production environments. Experience in system or software architecture, implementation, or verification and validation of complex embedded systems. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce precise technical documentation. Our systems operate with distributed control, dynamic routing, and real-time responsiveness, enabling sustained advantage across complex mission environments. About the role Forterra is looking for a Lead Software Test Engineer to establish and run verification and validation for the safety critical embedded software used on our autonomous ground vehicles. This is initially an individual contributor role. You will set the software test approach, build the automation and test environments, execute the work, and maintain the evidence needed for customer and safety reviews. You will work closely with software, systems, and safety engineers to find problems early and make sure the software behaves correctly when things go wrong. As the capability grows, the role may develop into a technical lead for a small test team Someone who can build a practical software test capability from the ground up and is comfortable working directly in the code, test environments, and evidence. This person should be able to work across software, systems, and safety engineering while staying focused on finding meaningful failures and making the product more dependable What you'll do Set the verification and validation approach for safety critical embedded software from kickoff through qualification, including the test plan, test procedures, results, and reports. Turn system, software, and safety related requirements into practical tests with objective pass or fail criteria. Maintain traceability between requirements, tests, results, and anomalies. Build and maintain automated test frameworks for embedded software, including software in the loop and hardware in the loop environments. Exercise failure behavior through fault injection, timing and jitter tests, communications failures, memory faults, power and clock faults, negative tests, boundary tests, and stress tests. Use static analysis, dynamic analysis, and coverage results to find gaps and help the team close them. Prepare and maintain test evidence, including plans, procedures, results, V&V matrices, compliance matrices, anomaly records, tool qualification records, and contributions to the safety case. Work with software, systems, and safety engineers to review designs for testability, improve requirements, and support technical reviews and assessments. Provide technical guidance through test plan reviews, design reviews, pairing, and mentoring. Help establish the practices and infrastructure needed to grow a small software test capability. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered. Five or more years of experience testing embedded systems or safety critical software. Strong working knowledge of C or C++ and Python for test automation. Experience working with requirements management and requirements traceability using tools such as Jama or DOORS. Familiarity with MISRA C or MISRA C++, static analysis, and structural coverage methods such as branch coverage and MC/DC. Experience testing software on an RTOS such as QNX, including work with embedded targets, debuggers, and instrumentation. Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to separate hardware, software, and firmware problems in a complex system. A practical, organized approach to managing several priorities and producing clear technical documentation. Ability to work remotely with up to 25% travel Preferred Qualifications Experience applying safety critical development and assurance standards such as ISO 26262, IEC 61508, DO-178C, MIL-STD-882E, JSSSEH, or JS-SSA-IG. Experience with QNX, Linux, NXP S32G, or similar embedded platforms. Experience with CAN, CAN-FD, Ethernet, UDS, J1939, or other vehicle networks and diagnostic protocols. Understanding of robotics domains such as motion control, planning, perception, fault management, and vehicle interfaces. Experience integrating electromechanical systems in automotive, aerospace, medical, industrial, defense, or similar environments. Experience providing technical leadership through design reviews, mentoring, or improvements to shared test and development practices. Description: IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN ’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC. With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way: responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in. Platform Engineering builds what the rest of IREN builds on. We own data engineering, automation, developer tooling, AI enablement, and product engineering, the systems that turn a fleet of data centers and GPU clusters into a platform our customers and our own teams can move quickly on. Much of it is being built now, for the first time, so there is no legacy stack to maintain and no established playbook to follow. This is one of the most senior technical roles at IREN , and it is an individual contributor role. A staff engineer is not a manager without reports. The scope is the organisation rather than a single team. The problems you take on are the ones that cross several teams, that no one team can solve alone, and that will still matter in three years. We expect you to think in years rather than sprints. Part of the job is holding a view of where the platform needs to be well beyond the current roadmap, making the case for it, and then sequencing the work so teams can move toward it while still shipping. You will write the design documents other teams build against, and you will be measured on whether they turned out to be right. The clearest way a staff engineer creates value here is through other engineers, so we are looking for someone who coaches at the scale of the organisation rather than the team they sit with. That means design and architecture review across teams, pairing on the problems people are stuck on, writing the things that teach, and delivering large pieces of work by growing the engineers who build them rather than building it all yourself. We expect deep expertise in at least one domain, and we expect you to see past organisational boundaries: to notice when two teams are solving the same problem twice, when the right fix sits outside your area, and when the honest answer is that something should not be built at all. We look for a customer centric view throughout. In Platform Engineering the customer is usually another team at IREN , and the test of a design is whether it makes their work easier, not whether it is elegant. Responsibilities Own the technical direction of an area spanning several teams, on a horizon measured in years rather than quarters. Raise the level of engineers across the organisation: design and architecture review beyond your own team, pairing on hard problems, and writing that teaches. Deliver large pieces of work by growing the engineers who build them, rather than building everything yourself. Take on the problems that cross team boundaries and that no single team owns, including the ones nobody has escalated yet. Write the design documents and technical standards other teams build against. Be the company's depth in your domain, and make that depth available rather than holding it. Prototype to settle open questions, so decisions rest on evidence rather than on argument. Stay hands on. Write and review code, debug production problems, and carry the pager for what you own. Find where the organisation is slow, and fix the technical causes of it. Work with engineering managers and product on planning and sequencing, including what the organisation should stop doing. Requirements 10 or more years of professional software engineering experience, several of them at senior level or beyond. Deep expertise in at least one domain, for example distributed systems, databases and storage, networking, data engineering, or applied AI systems, at the level where you are the person others come to. A record of technical influence beyond your own team, where the outcome depended on people you did not manage. Coaching at scale. Be ready to name engineers who grew because of you, and to describe what changed in how they work. Evidence of multi-year technical judgement: a direction you set, why you set it, and how it held up afterwards. Excellent written communication. Your design documents persuade people who were not in the room, and remain useful a year later. Experience owning systems in production, including operations, on-call, and incident response. A customer centric approach, and the discipline to check that a design makes someone's work easier rather than assuming it does. Comfort with ambiguity, including the judgement to say that something should not be built. Nice to have: Experience at a company scaling quickly, where the architecture had to change as it grew. Experience with high volume data pipelines, streaming systems, or telemetry and time series data. Experience putting machine learning or LLM systems into production. Experience working close to physical infrastructure, where the software must account for hardware that fails. Open source contributions, published work, or talks in your domain. These offerings are part of our broader Total Rewards package, thoughtfully designed to support your health, well-being, and long-term success. The role, in a nutshell Chainguard Containers is our core product, and this team builds it. As Principal Software Engineer in Container Product Engineering you will be the most senior individual contributor on a team of about fifteen engineers, setting the technical direction for the product and leading its largest, most consequential projects from idea to customer. Chainguard is growing explosively. Every line of code is now written with AI in the loop, which means the foundation it runs on has to be secure by default. You will shape that foundation: the hardened container images, the registry that serves them, and the tooling that lets engineers and AI agents adopt them. This is a technical leadership role, not a management role. You will work directly with engineering and product leaders to form the roadmap, then lead engineers across sub-teams to execute it. You will stay hands-on: you write and review code every week, and the hardest problems land on your desk first. What the team owns Product features for Chainguard Containers. Letting customers push their own images to our registry, Custom Assembly (customers compose images from our hardened packages), Helm charts, notifications, and compliance views such as STIG dashboards (STIG is the US government's hardening standard). The image build pipeline. The systems that turn packages from Wolfi, our Linux distribution, into signed and attested container images at scale, including moving image builds onto our own runner infrastructure. Registry performance and distribution. Work such as lazy loading, so a container starts before its whole image has downloaded, and image signing with Sigstore. Adoption tooling for engineers and AI agents. Migration tools that convert existing Dockerfiles to Chainguard Containers, and MCP servers (Model Context Protocol, the standard that lets AI agents call tools) so agents can discover and pull our images directly. What you'll do Set the technical direction for Chainguard Containers: the architecture of the build pipeline, the registry, and the adoption tooling over the next one to three years, written down and defended in the open. Form the roadmap with engineering and product leaders, then execute it. Turn ambiguous business goals into sequenced, staffed technical plans, and own the delivery of the largest multi-team projects from concept through production and adoption. Make and own the trade-offs that shape the product: build versus buy, when to re-platform and when not to, what to cut to hit a date. Write the decision down and bring dissenting engineers along. Lead through other engineers. Set the design bar, review the designs and code that matter most, and grow the Staff and Senior engineers around you into the next generation of technical leaders. Work with AI coding agents as part of how you build, review, and operate, and set the standard for how the whole team uses them safely as volume grows. Follow a problem wherever it goes: another team's service, a customer escalation, a support ticket, or go-to-market data, and work across team and company boundaries to get ahead of planning cycles. Represent Chainguard in the container and open source ecosystem: upstream work, standards conversations, talks, and the customer conversations where credibility is the product. Keep the systems you own healthy: observability, on-call, and the structural fixes that stop whole classes of incidents. What we're looking for 10+ years building and operating software that paying customers use, including several years as the technical lead of large, multi-team projects at a startup or a company in hyper-growth. Closely relevant experience in what we do: container images, container registries and the OCI image format (Open Container Initiative, the standard for container images and registries), Linux distributions or package management, build systems, or software supply chain security. Known in the field. Your work is visible outside your employer: open source you maintain, standards you helped shape, talks or writing that other engineers cite, or systems the industry knows you built. A track record of technical leadership without authority: you have set direction for a team you did not manage, and the team delivered. Experience forming and executing roadmaps with engineering and product leaders, including saying no, re-sequencing, and holding a date. Judgment on trade-offs at the product level. You have made calls that moved a company's roadmap, and you can show what you gave up and why. A systems thinker who designs for the whole path, from upstream source through build, signing, distribution, and the customer's runtime, and who sees second-order effects before they land. High agency and urgency. You find a way, you do not wait to be unblocked, and you unblock others. AI-native in how you build and lead. You use agentic coding tools daily and you have changed how a team works because of them. Architectural depth in Go: you can design a Go service from scratch, plus strong API design, databases and caching, and cloud infrastructure on GCP or AWS. Low ego. You do what you say and say what you do, and you communicate early when the news is bad. Excellent written English and experience leading on a distributed, remote-first team. Nice to haves Deep software supply chain security background: SBOMs (software bill of materials), Sigstore signing, or SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts, a framework for build integrity). Maintainer of, or significant contributor to, Chainguard 's open-source tools (Wolfi, apko, melange) or neighboring projects such as containerd, Kubernetes, or OCI specifications. Experience taking a product from early customers to broad adoption. Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code experience. A non-traditional path into engineering. We value people who learned by building. Location Remote. United States preferred; Open to Canada, the United Kingdom, and Germany. Description: Senior Web Developer – WordPress, Performance & Attribution $2,500 to $4,000 USD per month, depending on experience. Open to going higher for an exceptional candidate. Remote. Pacific Time Zone. Heads up: a video application is required to be considered. Resume + a short video interview through HireFlix. Both required. No video, no consideration. 👉 Start your video application here👈 Who this is for This role is for the developer who's tired of being a ticket-taker. Tired of fighting through three layers of project managers to ship a single page. Tired of pushing for a performance fix and watching it die in a backlog. Tired of doing the best work of your career inside an agency where the client never even learns your name. You'll work directly with the founder. When you see something on the site that's slow, broken, or underperforming, you can fix it. When you have a strong opinion about how to architect something, you'll be heard. The website is your domain. You own it, you ship it, you make it better every week. If you love rolling up your sleeves and shipping work every day, this is for you. If you want to lead a team or build strategy from 30,000 feet, this isn't. About us We're a residential plumbing company based in Orange County, California. We've built a strong brand serving homeowners across Southern California, and we're investing heavily in organic growth. This role is a key part of that investment. Your first project: site rebuild Your first major project is leading the rebuild of doitrightplumbers.com on our existing stack (WordPress, Hello Elementor, Elementor Pro, WP Engine, Cloudflare). Not a content refresh. A ground-up rebuild focused on performance, conversion, and a scalable component system that supports rapid landing page production. Scope includes migration planning with zero SEO loss, a reusable component library, Core Web Vitals targets met before launch, full GTM and GA4 rebuilt cleanly, and schema implementation across the new site. After launch, you transition into ongoing ownership. What you'll own Website development. Building and maintaining our WordPress site, shipping new landing pages, location pages, and service pages on demand. Expected publishing cadence after launch: 3 to 5 new pages per week using the component library. Page speed and Core Web Vitals. This is the heart of the role. LCP, INP, CLS, PageSpeed scores. Continuous monitoring, image optimization, script auditing, caching strategy. Slow pages are not acceptable. Cloudflare and WP Engine. Cache rules, page rules, security settings, firewall configuration, staging environments, plugin audits, security updates. You own the platform, not just the pages. Schema implementation. The SEO specialist defines schema strategy. You handle JSON-LD implementation, structured data testing, deployment, and validation across LocalBusiness, Service, FAQPage, Review, and BreadcrumbList types. Analytics and attribution. GTM, GA4, conversion tracking across Google Ads, Bing, Facebook, Reddit, and WhatConverts. When tracking breaks, you diagnose and fix it. Attribution is a craft, not an afterthought. Technical SEO foundation. Sitemaps, robots.txt, crawl budget, canonicals, 301 redirects, indexation issues, Search Console error resolution. Conversion rate optimization. Continuous A/B testing on hero sections, forms, CTAs, and page layouts. Mobile-first development and accessibility. Most of our customers convert on mobile. Every page is built mobile-first. WCAG 2.1 AA compliance expected. How you work with the team You'll partner closely with our Senior SEO Specialist. They own the strategy (content, link building, schema specs, internal linking strategy). You own the technical surface that brings it to life. Daily Slack collaboration, weekly working session, clean handoff process. You'll also have a weekly working session with our CMO and direct access to the founder. No agency layer. No buried management chain. What you need to have 5+ years of hands-on web development experience. You've shipped real work and you can prove it. Deep WordPress and Elementor Pro fluency. You build in Elementor every day and know its limits. PHP fluency. You can write custom functions, build custom post types, and modify themes when Elementor isn't enough. Real Cloudflare and WP Engine experience. You've configured cache rules, firewalls, staging environments, and managed production sites end to end. Real attribution and analytics chops. GTM, GA4, conversion tracking across multiple ad platforms. You can debug a broken pixel. Schema implementation expertise. JSON-LD, structured data testing, the technical knowledge to deploy and validate. Page speed obsession. You can walk us through specific optimizations you made and the before/after metrics that resulted. Site migration experience. You've led at least one full WordPress rebuild without losing rankings, conversions, or tracked attribution. Home services or local business website experience. This is a must. We want people who've shaped real local businesses, not Fortune 500 division work. Strong written English and Pacific Time Zone hours. We're not interested in candidates who plan to flip their schedule for this role. A note on how we work This is a 100% remote role. We don't use monitoring software and we don't micromanage. We trust our team to do excellent work and communicate proactively. That trust runs both ways. Show up, take ownership, operate with high integrity. This role is full-time. Not a side gig. Your full attention during business hours is part of what we're paying for. Hours and compensation Full-time, 100% remote Monday to Friday, 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM Pacific Time One-hour lunch and two 10-minute breaks $2,500 to $4,000 USD per month, DOE. Independent contractor through our global payroll partner Reports to: CMO and Founder Start date: Immediate How to apply To be considered, submit both: Your resume through this BambooHR posting A short video interview through our HireFlix link below The video is 4 questions, about 15 minutes from your phone or laptop. A real person watches every video. 👉 Start your video application here👈 Applications without a completed video will not be reviewed. Resume alone is not enough. Finalists will be asked for a custom screen-share video walking through their actual workflow and 2 to 3 live WordPress sites they've built. That's the deep dive. The HireFlix video is the gate. Salary: $2,500 to $3,500 USD per month Originally posted on Himalayas

Description: Why Thunderbird? Thunderbird is one of the world’s most trusted open-source email applications, empowering more than 20 million people globally. At Thunderbird, we build privacy-respecting communication and productivity tools that help people manage their digital lives while staying in control of their data. We are open source by design. Our products are developed transparently and in collaboration with a global community of contributors, and that same spirit shapes how we work: collaboratively, inclusively, and with a shared commitment to putting users first. Our small but growing distributed team includes more than 65 people across seven countries. As Thunderbird evolves beyond a single desktop application, we are expanding across desktop, mobile, paid services, AI offerings, and enterprise-facing work to build independent, privacy-respecting alternatives to big tech ecosystems. Our revenue model combines user donations, which help keep Thunderbird’s applications freely available, with paid services that cover the costs of hosted offerings while supporting long-term sustainability and continued innovation. A note about Thunderbird and Mozilla : Thunderbird Technologies Corporation is the nonprofit-owned company behind Thunderbird email and a growing portfolio of products. While part of the Mozilla family, Thunderbird is a separate entity from Mozilla Corporation and Mozilla Foundation with its own compensation programs, benefits, and employment policies. To learn more, visit The opportunity As a Staff Software Engineer, Services, you’ll help shape the architecture and technical direction of web-based products that extend Thunderbird beyond email. The Services team is currently focused on building offerings such as an appointment calendar and secure file storage and transfer solutions, creating valuable experiences for our users while supporting additional revenue streams for Thunderbird. This is a Staff-level individual contributor role with significant technical ownership and influence. You’ll work with designers, engineers, and community members to write code, build prototypes, solve complex problems, and make technical decisions that shape our products. You’ll take a holistic view of our code and systems, helping establish the architecture and software patterns that allow our Services products to evolve and scale. You’ll also take on broad, ambiguous problems that have a direct impact on our goals, from improving our technical architecture to helping grow Services users and subscribers. Along the way, you’ll provide technical and product direction across teams, mentor other engineers, and identify ways to make our systems and processes more sustainable, scalable, and easier to work with. What you’ll do Lead the technical architecture of new Services products, taking ownership of complex projects and identifying improvements that strengthen our systems as they evolve. Write code, build prototypes and experiments, and contribute throughout the development lifecycle, from planning and testing through implementation, monitoring, and maintenance. Help establish software patterns and make technical decisions across our Services products, including investigating and proposing technology choices. Build and evolve analytics and infrastructure that help the team use user-generated data to inform decisions. Take on ambiguous, high-level problems with broad scope and direct impact on Services goals, including growing users and subscribers. Provide technical and product direction across Thunderbird and lead technical collaboration with other parts of Mozilla and community contributors when needed. Work closely with the team and community to surface issues, refine ideas, and develop practical solutions. Identify and plan improvements that make our systems and processes more accessible, self-serviceable, lower friction, sustainable, scalable, and easier to delegate. Mentor other engineers through code review, documentation, technical discussions, process improvements, and ongoing guidance. Stay current with evolving technologies, coding standards, libraries, and frameworks and apply that knowledge to your work. What you bring 10+ years of web software development experience, including experience designing scalable and efficient systems and launching complex web projects at scale. Expert-level JavaScript skills and knowledge of at least one additional programming language, such as Python, Rust, Go, or C++. An understanding of the business landscape, including challenges and opportunities, and experience collaborating with teams to expand Thunderbird’s user and donor base. Experience with front-end frameworks, full-stack development, and/or API development. Strong knowledge of software development practices, including testing, code review, and documentation, and the ability to help others develop these skills. Experience acting as a technical lead, solving complex technical problems, and providing mentorship and guidance to other engineers. Experience collaborating remotely across disciplines such as engineering, product management, QA, and design. Excellent written and verbal English communication and documentation skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and concisely with an international, geographically distributed team. Comfort working in an open-source environment and a commitment to Mozilla values. Ability to learn, evaluate, and responsibly use emerging technologies, including AI-enabled tools, to improve work processes. A commitment to continuous learning and staying current with industry trends and technologies. Ability and willingness to travel periodically, including internationally. Bonus points for Experience with product management or product-focused work. What success looks like Success in this role will look like a strong technical leader who not only helps the Web Services team grow, but also has a direct hand in helping Thunderbird grow and evolve our product offerings. Over time, your work will help: Grow & mature scalable, modern software patterns and architecture across Web Services products. Turn new product ideas and complex technical problems into working solutions, prototypes, and experiments. Partner with leadership and cross-functional partners (Product, Design, etc) to help generate data-driven product decisions. Provide clear technical and product direction across complex, cross-functional work. Help other engineers grow their technical, collaboration, and leadership skills. Support the growth of users and subscribers as Thunderbird expands its offerings beyond email. Work environment This is a full-time, fully remote position. You’ll join a distributed team of Thunderbird staff, open-source community members, and contributors from around the world. We rely on clear communication, thoughtful documentation, and collaborative decision-making to work effectively across time zones and disciplines. In this role, you’ll collaborate closely with designers, engineers, cross-functional teams across Thunderbird, other parts of Mozilla , and community contributors. Compensation & benefits We benchmark our base salaries to local markets and target the 60th percentile of the peer market. The salary ranges for this role are: Canada: $155,000 - $190,000 CAD We may consider candidates with strong skills but less than the required experience. Title, level and compensation will be determined based on qualifications and experience. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your whole self. Work & career Fully remote work & schedule flexibility Company-provided laptop Annual bonus program Monthly remote work stipend Annual professional development stipend Access toCoursera learning platform Industry conferences Company all-hands and team gatherings Rest & play 24 days PTO per year (prorated) Your birthday Year-end company shutdown 9 wellbeing days Public holidays Other paid leave Quarterly wellbeing stipend for personal / family activities Health & family RRSP contributions Health, dental, & vision insurance Disability insurance Life insurance Employee assistance program Paid parental leave Paid sick days Work eligibility Applicants must reside in and have permanent work authorization for the country location(s) specified in the posting. Description: Description Sprout Social is looking to hire a Staff Software Engineer, Web to the Engineering team. Why join Sprout’s Engineering team ? Sprout empowers over 30,000 global brands to harness the power of social media, operating on a true "tech-giant" scale. Every day, our engineering infrastructure processes tens of billions of requests and asynchronous events, ingests billions of social messages, and drives over 1,000 production deployments every month, all while embedding cutting-edge AI directly into our platform. Sprout Engineering sits at the intersection of massive scale, technical craft, and tight-knit collaboration across mobile, front-end, back-end, and site reliability engineering. Instead of being a small cog in a massive machine, you’ll solve complex distributed systems problems alongside exceptional peers in an environment built for high autonomy and fast execution. Because our platform is a multi-product suite, you have the unique opportunity to explore new technologies, shift across domains, and continuously diversify your skills without ever needing to change companies—accelerating your career while making a direct impact on our customers every single day. What you’ll do Write clean, performant, and maintainable code. Provide technical leadership and guidance to other team members, including junior engineers. Work closely with cross-functional teams, including backend developers, designers, and product managers, to deliver world class customer experiences. Participate in and conduct code reviews to maintain code quality, provide feedback, and ensure adherence to coding standards. Continuously improve the codebase by identifying areas for refactoring and optimization to enhance maintainability and scalability. What you’ll bring We’re looking for a creative, highly motivated, and inquisitive learner to build great software with us. If you confidently write web applications using TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML and CSS, we’d love to talk with you! The minimum qualifications for this role include: 7+ years of experience with planning, building, and releasing frontend applications with web technologies (React, JavaScript, TypeScript) Experience building web applications with TypeScript Preferred qualifications for this role include: Experience working as a full stack engineer. Experience working with Node.js Experience working in a large codebase Experience building and/or maintaining an internal UI library Communication and project management skills from collaborating with people across different teams and functional areas. How you’ll grow Within 1 month, you’ll plant your roots, including: Complete Sprout’s New Hire training program alongside other new Sprout team members. Deliver business value by shipping your first code change with active pairing/mentoring from your teammates. Learn how code is deployed to our end users through collaboration with front end developers on your team. Have a firm understanding of the team’s roadmap and the team’s Agile processes by having discussions with your team’s manager. Within 3 months, you’ll start hitting your stride by: Independently own and deliver the front end part of small to medium features without peer consultation Adhere to the team’s engineering best practices, such as testing expectations, shared patterns, and documentation. Openly communicate with all disciplines of the team, including back-end engineers, product design and product managers, in order to move the team’s work forward. Contribute to team processes by participating in team activities, such as code review, estimation, technical specification planning, collaboration in requirements definition, and contribution of feedback during retrospectives. Within 6 months, you’ll be making a clear impact through: Author a technical specification plan for a roadmap project and collaborate with teammates to create an agreed upon delivery plan. Mentor junior teammates to provide guidance and coaching on code implementation, design review, and other software engineering and Agile practices. Understand how the team uses React and Typescript frameworks and be comfortable explaining relevant details to other engineers. Collaborate effectively with product managers to ensure that projects are delivered on time and with quality. Understand the how we structure, build and deploy the apps and be comfortable explaining relevant details to other engineers. Have knowledge of your team’s target customer base and their most common use cases within the application. Within 12 months, you’ll make this role your own by: Have an understanding of all aspects of our web application, including every module, less common use cases and all the Personas within our user base. Demonstrate end-to-end responsibility for delivering roadmap projects on time, from technical planning to performing/guiding implementation to testing to final delivery. Balance the continuum of trade-offs during code design, knowing that solutions can favor faster delivery with less strict technical requirements or solutions can favor future technical maintainability with delayed delivery of customer value. Identify a technical initiative (e.g. technical debt, introduction of a new system, need for a new JavaScript dependency, performance improvement, etc) for your team. Of course what is outlined above is the ideal timeline, but things may shift based on business needs and other projects and tasks could be added at the discretion of your manager.
